name: Pregabalin

lead: Pregabalin (Lyrica) is a prescription gabapentinoid approved for neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia and add-on seizure treatment, and licensed for generalized anxiety disorder in some regions. On looksmax.org, users describe taking it to feel less inhibited and appear more relaxed and confident socially.

It binds the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, reducing release of excitatory neurotransmitters such as glutamate. User accounts are anecdotal; no trial has tested it for social presence in people without a diagnosed condition.

paras: Forum users describe taking it before social situations to ease inhibition, and some swap questions about obtaining it and about withdrawal. Medically it is taken on a prescribed schedule for its approved conditions.

The label warns of respiratory depression with other CNS depressants, suicidal thoughts, angioedema, dizziness, somnolence, peripheral edema, weight gain and withdrawal reactions after abrupt stopping. It is Schedule V in the US, and reference sources note misuse potential.

angle.text: Forum posters take pregabalin to lower social anxiety and inhibition, aiming to come across as more relaxed, outgoing and confident. It is approved for nerve pain, fibromyalgia and seizures.

lead: Pregabalin is a prescription gabapentinoid, a drug structurally related to the neurotransmitter GABA, sold by Pfizer as Lyrica and under many other brand names. It is licensed for neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia and add-on treatment of partial seizures, and in some regions for generalized anxiety disorder [1][2][3]. In looksmaxxing communities its place is about confidence and presentation: users describe taking it to feel calmer and less inhibited when talking to people or going on dates, on the reasoning that looking good matters less if social anxiety stops a person from showing up, making eye contact or holding a conversation [4][5].

The drug works by binding the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, which is thought to reduce the release of excitatory neurotransmitters such as glutamate. It does not act on GABA receptors despite the structural resemblance [1][3][6]. Silverman and colleagues at Northwestern University synthesized it around 1990 as a successor to gabapentin; the US FDA approved it in December 2004 [3].

Research on pregabalin is extensive for the conditions it is licensed for. Large meta-analyses and guidelines place it among first-line options for several kinds of neuropathic pain [7][8][9], and a 2019 network meta-analysis of drug treatments for generalised anxiety disorder included it among the agents compared [10]. No published trial has tested it for social disinhibition or appearance outcomes in people without a diagnosed condition. Its US label carries warnings on respiratory depression with other central nervous system depressants, suicidal thoughts, angioedema and withdrawal after abrupt discontinuation, and it is a Schedule V controlled substance in the US and Class C in the UK [2][3][6].

subs.h: Use in appearance and social contexts
paras: Pregabalin is not marketed for appearance. Its connection to looksmaxxing is through social ease: forum posters who describe high inhibition or social anxiety discuss it as a way to talk to women, go out at night or attend events with less fear [4][5]. One widely read looksmax.org post describes a student who obtained a prescription by explaining social anxiety to a clinic physician, then reported feeling relaxed, tipsy-like, talkative and free of worry on the first days of use [4]. Other thread titles describe 'insane night out' experiences, ask whether it affects sexual stamina, and call it among the best drugs a poster has tried [11][12][13]. These are personal accounts.

Communities also discuss routes of access, including prescriptions and purchases outside pharmacies; the wiki does not document sourcing. Clinicians and regulators describe non-prescribed use as misuse with risks of dependence, interaction and withdrawal [3][6].

The current US label lists diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain, postherpetic neuralgia, fibromyalgia, neuropathic pain associated with spinal cord injury and adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients from one month of age [2]. Reference sources report that fibromyalgia was the first condition for which the FDA approved a drug [3]. In the European Union and some other regions pregabalin is also licensed for generalized anxiety disorder, and a controlled-release form, Lyrica CR, was approved in the US in 2017 for diabetic neuropathy and postherpetic neuralgia [3].

Off-label uses discussed in clinical literature include restless legs syndrome, perioperative pain and anxiety, and chronic cough, where a European Respiratory Society guideline considered gabapentinoids [14][15][16].

Pregabalin binds with high affinity to the alpha-2-delta subunit of presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels. Rather than blocking the channel directly, this binding is thought to reduce calcium influx and the release of excitatory neurotransmitters including glutamate, noradrenaline and substance P; the exact route to its pain, seizure and anxiety effects is not fully established [1][6]. Despite being a GABA analogue, it does not bind GABA receptors [3].

A 2010 review comparing pregabalin and gabapentin reported that pregabalin is absorbed in a predictable, dose-proportional way, while gabapentin absorption is saturable [17]. Wikipedia reports oral bioavailability of at least 90 percent, negligible plasma protein binding, an elimination half-life of roughly six hours, and excretion of about 98 percent of recovered drug unchanged in urine, so the dose is reduced in people with reduced kidney function [3]. Pregabalin is described as roughly 2.5 times more potent than gabapentin in clinical studies [6].

A 2003 randomised placebo-controlled trial in postherpetic neuralgia and a 2004 double-blind trial in painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy were among the pivotal studies that supported approval for neuropathic pain [18][19]. The 2015 Lancet Neurology systematic review and meta-analysis by the Neuropathic Pain Special Interest Group of the International Association for the Study of Pain analysed 229 randomised double-blind studies and, using GRADE, produced recommendations in which gabapentinoids including pregabalin are among the first-line drug groups for neuropathic pain; the authors estimated publication bias may overstate treatment effects by about 10 percent [7]. The European Federation of Neurological Societies guideline and a 2007 evidence-based recommendation paper likewise rank pregabalin among first-line agents [8][9].

Two multicentre trials compared pregabalin with other drugs or combinations in diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain: the COMBO-DN study of high-dose duloxetine versus pregabalin versus combination, and the OPTION-DM randomised trial of sequenced combinations with amitriptyline and duloxetine [20][21].

For anxiety, a 2019 Lancet systematic review and network meta-analysis of drug treatments for generalised anxiety disorder (89 trials) assessed efficacy by change in Hamilton Anxiety Scale score and acceptability by discontinuation rates, and pregabalin was among the drugs compared [10]. A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis in Molecular Psychiatry of gabapentin and pregabalin in bipolar disorder, anxiety and insomnia found 55 double-blind randomised trials; across the anxiety spectrum there was a consistent but not universal advantage over placebo, with pregabalin reducing preoperative anxiety (standardised mean difference -0.55) [22].

Registered trials also include a Phase 2 dose-response study in restless legs syndrome, a Phase 3 trial of once-daily pregabalin for partial seizures in 325 participants, post-mastectomy pain studies and a Korean post-marketing surveillance study of 4,175 participants [15][23][24][16]. No studies were found testing pregabalin for social disinhibition, dating confidence or appearance outcomes in people without a diagnosed condition.

Dizziness and drowsiness are the most frequent effects, reported by more than one in ten users in clinical trials, with weight gain, blurred vision, euphoria and confusion also listed as common [3]. The US label also lists peripheral edema, angioedema and other hypersensitivity reactions, suicidal behavior and ideation, and respiratory depression, especially with other central nervous system depressants [2]. Grokipedia additionally reports sexual dysfunction, including decreased libido, erectile dysfunction and abnormal orgasm [1]. A published case report describes pregabalin-induced sexual disinhibition in a patient [25].

Wikipedia reports that in December 2019 the FDA warned of serious breathing problems with gabapentinoids in people with respiratory risk factors or who take opioids or other sedatives, and that a review of 49 submitted cases from 2012 to 2017 included 12 deaths [3]. A 2020 Scottish study cited there found that many recurrent gabapentinoid users were co-prescribed opioids or benzodiazepines [3].

The US label warns of withdrawal reactions after abrupt or rapid discontinuation and recommends tapering over at least a week, while other health services recommend slower tapering; symptoms can include insomnia, nausea, anxiety and, rarely, seizures [2][3]. Wikipedia reports that around 4 percent of trial participants noted euphoria, which contributed to US controlled-substance status, and describes abuse potential as low to moderate and dose-dependent [3][6]. Recreational use at multiples of clinical amounts is described as producing alcohol- or benzodiazepine-like effects, with tolerance developing quickly [6].

Forum threads include questions from users starting the drug about withdrawal, and replies in which members describe withdrawal from pills as severe [5]. Hacker News has carried discussions of press reports about deaths linked to the drug, which sit alongside regulatory data [26].

Richard Bruce Silverman first synthesized pregabalin in 1990 at Northwestern University as a successor to gabapentin, in a programme in which Ryszard Andruszkiewicz prepared the series of molecules between 1988 and 1990 [3]. Warner-Lambert chemists reported the first manufacturing process in 1997 under the code CI-1008 [3]. The European Union and the FDA approved it in 2004, and it reached the US market in autumn 2005 [3]. Northwestern holds the US patent, exclusively licensed to Pfizer [3].

Lyrica became one of Pfizer's biggest products, with roughly 14 billion dollars in reported global revenue, and Pfizer spent a record 24.6 million dollars on television advertising in January 2016 alone [3]. Pfizer pleaded guilty in a US case over illegal promotion of Lyrica and three other drugs, including promotion for unapproved uses, and paid a record 2.3 billion dollar fine [3]. Generic pregabalin has been sold in the US since July 2019 [3].

Pregabalin is a Schedule V controlled substance in the US [1][3]. In the UK, the Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs recommended control in January 2016 and pregabalin and gabapentin became Class C drugs in April 2019, with prescriptions required to state the dose [3][6]. Australia lists it as prescription-only (Schedule 4) and added boxed warnings on abuse and dependence in 2021; Norway places it on a prescription schedule alongside benzodiazepines; Canada does not classify it as controlled [3][6]. Wikipedia reports a rise in Australian pregabalin-related deaths from 16 in 2013 to 121 in 2016 [3].

On looksmax.org, pregabalin appears in the 'low inhibition' and social-anxiety discussion rather than in appearance-enhancement threads. Typical threads are results posts after obtaining a prescription, questions about withdrawal, reports from nights out, questions about its effect on sexual stamina, and threads asking where to obtain it [4][5][11][12][27]. Posters use terms like 'high inhib' to describe people whose anxiety prevents them from acting socially. Some who discuss it have a prescription for anxiety; others discuss obtaining it without one.
